name: Do bathroom plumbing relocations require waterproofing changes too?

mainEntity.name: Do bathroom plumbing relocations require waterproofing changes too?
mainEntity.text: Do bathroom plumbing relocations require waterproofing changes too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom plumbing relocations often require waterproofing changes because the plumbing and waterproofing systems are tightly connected. If the shower drain, tub drain, or floor plumbing moves, the surrounding waterproofing usually needs to be rebuilt so water is directed correctly and penetrations are sealed in the right places. Even a vanity move can affect wall finishes if supply and drain locations shift inside the wet area. In shower remodels, waterproofing is especially critical because the new drain location, curb, pan slope, and wall membrane all have to work together. Skipping or minimizing these details can lead to leaks, tile failure, and costly repairs later. Homeowners should ask whether the plumbing relocation includes waterproofing coordination or whether that will be handled separately. The best remodels treat plumbing rough-in and waterproofing as one integrated step, not two unrelated jobs.
